requirements.requirement: Same-owner command context, source navigation eligibility and history-clone admission must pass before clone.
A live source follows clone and adoption into a newly generated browserTabId; the original source page is not explicitly destroyed by this callable.
The destination is announced with clone WebContents ID and lease; requested back/forward/reload is deferred through initialHistoryNavigation.
Destroyed or unadoptable destinations and invalid leases must not produce successful destination messages; close/destroy and pending cleanup follow the saved branches.
Only an absent live source plus reload can take the saved cold-restore/fresh path; back/forward cannot silently use it.
Route/host generation, session partition, preload/security preferences, navigation owner and lifecycle admission must remain consistent across the real host.

Source and destination history, back/forward/reload behavior, form state, loading/error behavior and post-clone independence need a candidate-runtime test and an original-behavior comparison where unavailable.
Whether Owl native clone copies JS heap, renderer process state or additional session state is unknown from these first-party source units.
requirements.restriction: A synthetic clone and absence of caller reads do not prove native absence. Public history losing an edited heap value alone neither proves nor disproves required equivalence.

routes.rule: Do not discard solely because the public history probe lost an edited JS heap value; do not accept solely because it restored a form.

routes.reason: Independent distribution/source, target ABI and exact behavior are still unproven; the original installed runtime is not a qualified independent input.

publicHistoryObservation.limitation: Public primitive observation only; no Owl clone/adoption or full functional equivalence tested.

decision: Retain a bounded public-history adapter feasibility route while rejecting drop-in API compatibility and same-view transfer as a clone. Native Owl heap semantics remain unknown; no product equivalence or full runtime selection is claimed.

nextAction.question: Can the fixed public runtime's owned duplicate-history candidate preserve source independence and back/forward/reload behavior?
nextAction.limits: Only synthetic local pages and the already acquired public runtime; no original-client launch, personal data, network service or model submission.
nextAction.closure: Record entry/index/URL/form state in both source and destination before and after each navigation, ownership cleanup and failure. Keep unknown original native semantics explicit.
